transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-09
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes (recording pauses at ~00:18:00 for brief interruption)
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Elena (Moxie Dir ML), Samir (Infra), Priya (PM), Nora (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Goal: scope POC to validate throughput/latency/cost for Moxie's clinical triage model.
- Primary asks: characterize QPS/concurrency patterns, token mix, benchmark plan, security gating, timeline.
- Success criteria draft: p95 latency targets, sustained QPS, minimal accuracy regression vs baseline.

Topics:
- Workload signature (QPS, burstiness, token distribution)
- Benchmarks (steady-state, spike, tail latency)
- Deployment model (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private V P C)
- Security controls and logs (SOC2, SAML, KMS/H S M)
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript body:
00:00 Jordan: All right thanks everyone for joining, quick intros — Jordan from Redwood, Maya our SE, and then I think we have Elena, Samir, Priya and Nora on the customer side.
00:12 Elena: Hey thanks, were excited to scope this POC. Were trying to understand if we can move inference off our in-house cluster with predictable latency and lower ops overhead.
00:22 Maya: Cool, do you want to start with what a typical day looks like for request volume and any bursts? Even rough numbers help.
00:30 Priya: Yeah so primary traffic is clinical triage bot inside the patient portal. Baseline is about 6 QPS average, peak midday around 55 QPS, and we see short bursts up to 180 QPS when digest emails/notifications run — those bursts last 2-6 minutes.
00:48 Samir: Also important: we serve lots of short messages (patient question ~30-80 tokens) but responses are longer, typically 120-400 tokens depending on follow-ups. So input:output token ratio is roughly 1:3 to 1:5 for most sessions.
01:10 Maya: Great, that helps. Do you have any token distribution histogram or percentiles? Means/medians?
01:18 Elena: We can export a sample. Median input 60 tokens, 75th ~120 tokens, median output 210 tokens, tail at 900 tokens when we produce long instructions. We'll share anonymized samples.
01:32 Jordan: Ok, for the POC we normally ask for a 10k sample of real requests + an eval set of ~500 labeled cases for quality checks. That lets us run token-mix driven benchmarks and accuracy checks.
01:44 Priya: That works. Question — are you able to simulate warmed KV cache behavior? Our models use prefix caching heavily so cold-starts look different.
01:55 Maya: Yes, our traffic generator supports warm/cold cache modes; we'll warm the KV cache to simulate day-to-day latency and also run cold start spikes. Note sometimes the transcriber inserts spaces so K V cache appears in notes, sorry if that shows up.
02:10 Nora: Security question: we need to ensure data residency and logs. We're SOC2, and we need S A M L SSO, audit logs to our SIEM, and an option to bring your own K M S or H S M. Can Redwood support that in Dedicated or Private?
02:28 Jordan: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and V P C peering; Private on-prem is also an option for air-gapped, but thats a longer timeline and enterprise license. Well attach the security checklist and network diagram after the call.
02:40 Samir: For latency targets: product is sensitive to p95 — wed like p95 <= 300ms for short flows and <= 500ms for long flows, but we realize outputs are longer so that might be tough.
02:54 Maya: Helpful to separate token-limited latency (per-token generation) vs end-to-end request time. For hosted inference p95 under ~350-400ms on medium-size outputs is generally achievable on optimized A100-style backends with prefix caching and batching control. For Dedicated with pinned capacity we can target p95 sub-200ms depending on model size and quantization.
03:18 Elena: Wed like Redwoods recommendation: run benchmarks against your hosted endpoints first, then Dedicated if we need lower p95 or cost predictability.
03:29 Jordan: Yep, typical flow: Hosted quick benchmark to validate feasibility, then Dedicated pilot for sustained throughput and lower unit costs.
03:36 Maya: For the POC we'll propose three benchmark phases:
- Phase 1: 1-hour steady-state at target QPS (we recommend 20 QPS to start, representing a scaled sample of your traffic)
- Phase 2: Spike tests with short bursts to 200 QPS for 5 minutes to check autoscaling/fallbacks
- Phase 3: Tail-latency and cold-start matrix with warmed KV vs cold cache runs across different sequences
04:05 Priya: Can you also estimate cost per million tokens for Hosted vs Dedicated? We need a ballpark to justify to finance.
04:13 Jordan: We'll provide a cost model; rough ballpark during POC depends on batching, but we'll include token-level cost, infra overhead, and amortized cache benefit. We'll send a spreadsheet.
04:24 Samir: Regarding concurrency: our front-end maintains about 8 in-flight requests per session; system-wide concurrency during peak is about 220. So if you model concurrency, you need to account for frontend queuing and proxy timeouts.
04:40 Maya: Noted, well include concurrency in the load generator and model 502/504 patterns if queueing becomes high.
04:48 Elena: On evaluation — we need a pass/fail metric: accuracy regression under 2% on the labeled eval set, p95 lat < 350ms for 90% of flows, and no request error rate over 0.5% sustained.
05:05 Jordan: Thats a solid SLO set. We'll codify that in the POC charter.
05:12 Priya: Timeline question: how long to run the full POC from sample handoff?
05:18 Maya: Typical is 2-4 weeks: week 0 sample handoff + baseline checks; week 1 run benchmarks and iterate; week 2 validation and stakeholder review. If Dedicated or Private is chosen, add provisioning lead time (2-6 weeks for Dedicated capacity depending on region).
05:36 Samir: Are there any constraints on throughput shaping? We have burst budgets from our own infra team that might change concurrency.
05:45 Maya: We can define ingress shaping and enforce rate limits during the POC. Also will surface suggestions for batching and quantization to reduce token cost.
05:55 Elena: For long term were evaluating model variants — 7B vs 13B quantized — can Redwood run both for A/B to measure latency/quality tradeoffs?
06:06 Jordan: Yes we can route by policy and run A/B with automatic fallback to smaller models if latency breaches. We'll include model variants in the POC runway.
06:16 Priya: Anything else on security? Nora: We need audit logs forwarded to Splunk and role-based access; are logs available at token level?
06:25 Maya: We surface request/response metadata, latency, token counts, and redaction hooks. We do not store raw PII unless configured; we'll provide the log schema in the security packet.
06:37 Jordan: Quick recap and next steps — send benchmark template, security docs, schedule benchmark window, collect 10k samples, and sync on success criteria.
06:49 Elena: Sounds good, thanks.
06:53 Jordan: Great, well follow up via email with links: benchmark template (drive.google.com/drive/folder/benchmark-template-moxie), security checklist (redwood.com/security/moxie-checklist), and the proposed benchmark times.
07:07 (end)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels (Samir appears as Speaker 4 in auto transcript) and minor mis-hearings for acronyms (KMS -> K M S) — verified in recording.

Bench plan (raw summary inserted here):
- Samples: 10k user queries, anonymized, split 80/20 train/eval.
- Steady-state: 1h at 20 QPS (token mix applied), measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, token counts.
- Spike test: 3x-9x bursts to 200 QPS for 5 min, observe autoscaling, throttling, fallbacks.
- Cold-start matrix: 10 cold starts per model variant, measure extra latency and failure modes.
- Quality: run eval set and compute top-level metrics and delta vs baseline (pass if <2% degradation).
- Deliverables: benchmark report, telemetry dashboards, cost estimate spreadsheet.

Success criteria (draft):
- Functional: end-to-end p95 latency <= 350ms for 80% of short flows, <= 600ms for long flows during steady-state; error rate <0.5%.
- Quality: model outputs within 2% of baseline eval metrics.
- Ops: Redwood provides logs/audit, SSO integration validated, and PII redaction confirmed.
- Business: Cost estimate acceptable to Finance (TBD).

End of transcript.
